correctness.rationale: The eleven points \(Q_i=(i:1:i^3)\) have exactly the expected 15 zero-sum collinear triples by the Vandermonde formula; all other 150 triple determinants are units. The normalized scheme has fourteen variables and fifteen dependent-minor equations. Twelve incidences reconstruct six projective points via transverse line intersections. For the remaining minors, an exact GF(11) calculation gives \(3G\), \((-2x+2z)G\), \((-2x+5z-3)G\) with factors units at \((4,9)\). Hence its localized defining ideal is \((G)\). Its translated equation is \(3u(v-u)+u^3+3u^2v-5uv^2-5v^3\), so the quadratic initial form has distinct linear factors: the completed local ring is \(k[[U,V]]/(UV)\). The bundled standard-library checker reproduced all identities. The claim is local only.

value.rationale: This first prime-level bad-characteristic example exposes an explicit split nodal degeneration in an eleven-point rank-three realization scheme, in sharp contrast to the known characteristic-zero smoothness theorem. The two tangent branches and local multiplicity are structural invariants of a motivated elliptic-matroid configuration, not an arbitrary slice or a known-table recomputation. It addresses a precisely excluded fiber of the 2026 modular correspondence without claiming a global modular interpretation.
